description: Team battle golden vectors (docs/battle-protocol.md §F, "Team battles"). Generated by protocol/scripts/gen-team-vectors.ts; never regenerate to make a failing port pass. Each log row follows logColumns; booleans are 0 or 1, and healed is -1 when nothing was healed.

cases.name: duel-matches-battle-json
cases.note: battle.json's baseline-no-skill as a one-on-one team battle. Must reproduce it exactly (side 0 loses in 6 rounds with 174 HP left); the test suites replay every other battle.json and equipment.json case the same way.

cases.name: melee-reach-and-front-line-collapse
cases.note: Defenders stand back (slot 0), mid (slot 1) and front (slot 2), so Focus would pick the back pet on a tie. A Melee physical strike only reaches the front line and a Reach one also the column behind it, while magic reaches anyone. When the front pet falls, the mid column becomes the front line.

cases.name: ranged-long-shot
cases.note: A Ranged physical strike on the back-line pet, beyond the front line, deals 85%. Pinned by the flag and by the fight changing at longShotPct 100.

cases.name: shell-and-sage-auras
cases.note: The front pet has a Shell neighbour and a Sage neighbour, so it takes hits at +10% DEF and +10% MDEF. Pinned by the fight changing at auraPct 100.

cases.name: combo-on-one-target
cases.note: Three Focus attackers on one front-line target. The second and third hits in a round carry combo 1 and 2, worth +10% and +20%.

cases.name: expose-after-cunning-crit
cases.note: A Cunning crit marks its target, and the next teammate to hit it deals 120% and spends the mark.

cases.name: tank-guards-a-neighbour
cases.note: A hit that would knock out the frail front pet lands on its Tank neighbour instead, once per battle.

cases.name: tailwind-from-swift-neighbours
cases.note: Two Swift neighbours add 2% crit chance each to the middle pet. Pinned by a crit that disappears at tailwindBps 0.

cases.name: fury-rally
cases.note: A Fury pet at full health strikes at +30% once a teammate has been knocked out.

cases.name: lifelink-heals-an-injured-neighbour
cases.note: A Bloodlust physical hit heals the most injured of itself and its neighbours: here the battered neighbour, which the Breaker defender goes after for its INT, not the striker.

cases.name: second-chance-for-a-teammate
cases.note: A Rebirth pet's second chance saves the first teammate knocked out, leaving it on 1 HP, and is spent.

cases.name: breaker-targets-highest-int
cases.note: Breaker goes for the highest-INT enemy in reach, here slot 1, where Focus would take slot 0 on the tie.

cases.name: hunter-targets-element-prey
cases.note: Hunter (element 0) goes for the enemy its element beats (element 1, slot 1) rather than the Focus pick.

cases.name: bodyguard-targets-the-last-hitter
cases.note: Bodyguard goes for whoever last hit its most injured teammate. Pinned by the fight changing when it plays Focus instead.

cases.name: temperament-suits-the-tactic
cases.note: A Brave pet playing Focus deals 105%; the flag shows on its strikes and the fight changes without the temperament.

cases.name: speed-order-puts-a-fast-shell-first
cases.note: Under the speed turn order the fastest pet acts first even when it is a Shell, which the int order would put last.

cases.name: thirty-rounds-hp-share
cases.note: Two walls that cannot finish each other in 30 rounds. The higher share of total HP left wins.

cases.name: thirty-rounds-exact-tie-goes-to-the-defender
cases.note: Both sides stand after 30 rounds with exactly the same share of HP left, so the defender wins.

cases.name: full-neutral-squads
cases.note: Three against three at launch settings: everyone Melee, int turn order, no temperament. Mixed skills, so several rules meet in one fight.

cases.name: full-geared-squads
cases.note: The neutral squads wearing equipment bonuses, with Bloodlust and Rebirth on the defending side.

cases.name: full-attributes-2-squads
cases.note: Every input Attributes 2.0 adds: the speed turn order, all three ranges, and temperaments that suit their tactics.

draws.name: ranks-in-roster-order-seed-1
draws.note: Roster pet i has rank i + 1.

draws.name: ranks-reversed
draws.note: The top-ranked pet is last in the roster, so rank and roster position are not confused.

draws.name: ranks-shuffled-other-seed
draws.note: Same roster, a seed that draws a different lineup.
